t: Number of Elapsed Seconds Between Two Times — Parse and Subtract
o: Both times are given as "HH:MM:SS" with endTime not earlier than startTime, so no day wraparound is involved. Convert each time to total seconds since midnight (HH*3600 + MM*60 + SS) and subtract. Example 1: 3600 - 3600 + 25 = 25. Example 2: (13*3600) - (12*3600 + 34*60 + 56) = 46800 - 45296 = 1504. Constraints are tiny; any parsing method works.
k: Convert each timestamp to seconds-since-midnight, then a single subtraction answers the query.
Since endTime >= startTime, no modular arithmetic or wraparound handling is needed.

a.i: Split each string on ':' (or slice fixed-width fields), interpret the three parts as integers, weight them by 3600, 60, 1, and subtract. This is the simplest correct solution.
s: Split startTime into h1, m1, sec1 and compute t1 = h1*3600 + m1*60 + sec1.
Do the same for endTime to get t2.

a.n: Approach 2: Manual digit extraction without split
a.i: Since the format is fixed-width, characters at indices 0-1, 3-4, 6-7 are always the digits. Computing values via character arithmetic avoids any library splitting and is marginally faster, though asymptotically identical.
s: Read hours as (c0-'0')*10 + (c1-'0'), minutes from indices 3-4, seconds from indices 6-7.
Combine into total seconds for both times.
a.t: O(1) — constant number of character reads.

w: Either approach is fine; prefer the split-based one for readability. Edge cases: equal times (answer 0), times crossing hour boundaries, and midnight-adjacent times — all handled automatically since endTime >= startTime guarantees a non-negative difference. A likely follow-up asks for the answer modulo 86400 when endTime may fall on the next day; then compute (t2 - t1 + 86400) % 86400.
